answer.rationale: Rollback is ruled out by the non-revertible security patch, so memory_b1 is not actionable. Circuit breaking would shed or fail writes and conflicts with the no-lost-writes objective. Read-replica routing helped write latency only when report/read load was the contended work; here the stated load is peak settlement writes, so that lever is weakly indicated. Regional failover has a prior latency-recovery win, but failing over the write path during daily settlement peak has unclear consistency/in-flight-write risk, so it is the alternate to check, not the first move. Adding capacity is the intervention most aligned with heavy write-path load and sustained availability without discarding customer writes. Memory_b3 is about headroom provisioned before a peak, not mid-incident, and the latency climb is also time-aligned with the new release, so root cause is not established—verify b3 and b2, scale as a standard experiment rather than a fleet-wide shift.
